title: What comes after one, seven, nineteen, thirty seven?
description: Four clusters of dots have one, seven, nineteen and thirty seven dots. The video finds the jumps between them, adds the next ring, and gets sixty one.
teaching_notes: One idea: the jumps of the sequence are the rings, and they grow by the same amount each time. Watch for students who add six again instead of the next bigger ring.

video_script.why: The child finds the rings that each cluster adds, sees that each ring is six dots longer than the one before, and adds the next ring.
video_script.substitution: The next number is the last number plus the next ring, and each ring is six dots bigger than the ring before.
video_script.anchor: four clusters of dots in a row with the numbers 1, 7, 19, 37 under them, and an empty frame after them
video_script.payoff_line: The next number is sixty one

final_answer.spoken: the next number is sixty one

maths_rules: the jumps are 6, 12, 18, so the next jump is 24
video_script.design: One idea: the rings are the jumps and they grow by the same amount. Callback to adding a ring of twelve around a cluster. Wrong idea: none is broken. The four clusters stay on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; four clusters of dots in a row with the numbers 1, 7, 19, 37 under them and an empty frame after them

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.clusters: the four clusters appear with the numbers under them
marks.ask: the empty frame appears with the words next number and its name

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about clusters of dots.
<bookmark mark='clusters'/>The clusters have one, seven, nineteen and thirty seven dots.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the next number, and what is this sequence called?

beats.on_screen: the four clusters hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a centre dot with a small ring, then the same cluster with a bigger ring around it

marks.ring: a ring appears around a cluster
marks.jump: the number of dots in the new ring is shown as the jump between two numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='ring'/>Each cluster adds a ring around the cluster before it.
<bookmark mark='jump'/>The dots of the new ring are the jump between the two numbers.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers one, seven, nineteen and thirty seven.

beats.on_screen: To find: the next number, and the name of the sequence

marks.find: the words next number and name are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the next number, and the name of the sequence.

marks.centre: the first cluster is shown as one centre dot
marks.rings: the rings of 6, 12 and 18 dots are outlined in turn

narration: <bookmark mark='centre'/>Step one, look at the rings. The first cluster is one centre dot.
<bookmark mark='rings'/>The rings that follow have six, twelve and eighteen dots.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, the jumps: 6, 12, 18, so the next jump is 24

marks.jumps: the jumps 6, 12 and 18 are written between the numbers
marks.next: the next jump, 24, is written with each jump six more than the one before

narration: <bookmark mark='jumps'/>Step two, find the next jump. The jumps are six, twelve and eighteen.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Each jump is six more than the one before, so the next jump is twenty four.

marks.ring: a fourth ring of twenty four dots is drawn around the last cluster

narration: <bookmark mark='ring'/>Step three, add the ring. A new ring of twenty four dots goes around the last cluster.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Thirty seven plus twenty four is sixty one.

marks.check: the centre dot and all four rings are added in one line and a tick appears after 61

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check by adding the centre dot and all four rings. One plus six plus twelve plus eighteen plus twenty four is sixty one.

marks.name: the words hexagonal numbers appear above the sequence

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The next number is sixty one.
<bookmark mark='name'/>The sequence is called hexagonal numbers, because each cluster has the shape of a hexagon.
